title: Preserve master retry action when an owner timer occupies the shared hydration retry slot
outcome: The shared hydration retry-timer slot follows independently agreed owner/master collision semantics without silently substituting an owner-only demand check for a master unloaded restart.
acceptance: Preserved fail-first evidence shows the master restart missing on unmodified d705038. An actual-source revert of the owed-bit behavior makes the new collision witness fail again, and restoring the source returns it to passing without a runtime fault switch or weakened assertions/timeouts. The full five-stage gate passes on the exact independently reviewed resulting input, with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding in the Codex/Claude read-only review pair.

Real-hook fake-timer witnesses reproduce an owner-read rejection followed by a master older-prefetch rejection inside its back-off. The existing timer performs exactly one optionless master restart and invokes the requester exactly once. A control closing owner demand before firing still performs the unloaded master restart without issuing an owner read; a control making the session fully loaded performs no master restart. Existing W1-W15/W5c, generated-model and proof-boundary checks continue to pass.

The existing per-session hydration retry-timer entry records one master-retry-owed bit. A master-originated ending requesting retry while the session is unloaded sets it whether creating a timer or finding one pending. On firing, an owed master restart runs first only if the session remains unloaded, without hydration options; the shared requester then runs once. Absorbed retry requests consume no retry attempt. Owner retry demand/cap behavior, base master retry eligibility, the existing shared timer slot and the Q7 backstop remain unchanged; no per-origin timers or additional registry are introduced.
